chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abu Ayyub from Abu Basir said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about 'the middle of what you feed your family,' and he said, 'That with which you sustain your dependents from the middle of that.' I said, 'And what is the middle of that?' He said, 'Vinegar, oil, dates, and bread, with which you satisfy them once.' I said, 'Their clothing?' He said, 'One garment.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: These are the narrations we mentioned recently regarding that the clothing is one garment; there is no contradiction between them and the earlier narrations because clothing is graded. So whoever is able to clothe them in two garments, it is upon him to do so; and whoever can only afford one garment, it is not obligatory upon him to do more than that. And when he is unable to do that as well as feeding, then fasting is upon him; and when he is unable to fast as well, then let him seek forgiveness from Allah, the Exalted and Mighty, and not repeat.
ai.seo_question: What is the hierarchy of expiation for breaking an oath in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi synthesizes these narrations to establish a graduated hierarchy of kaffarah, clarifying that the obligation to provide 'middle' sustenance and clothing is flexible based on individual financial capacity. The text concludes with a practical spiritual remedy for those unable to perform any of the physical acts, emphasizing that sincere repentance (istighfar) suffices when resources are exhausted.
